paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God is worth praising every single day, not just on the big ones. David was a king with a whole kingdom to run, and he still opened by calling God "my God and King" (Psalm 145:1). If a king had a King of his own, then that's a good reminder for the rest of us.

And look WHY David keeps praising. The LORD is "gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion" (Psalm 145:8). His compassion rests on all He has made, and He gives every living thing what it needs (Psalm 145:9, 16). Nobody has to earn a seat at that table, baker. I spent years in the back of a drawer, and I can tell you being found by a good King beats being polished by a bad one.

So what do we do with that? We lean in. "The LORD upholds all who fall and lifts up all who are bowed down" (Psalm 145:14), and He is "near to all who call on Him, to all who call out to Him in truth" (Psalm 145:18). Then we do what David did and pass it on, because one generation tells the next (Psalm 145:4). Your praise today is part of something that goes on "forever and ever" (Psalm 145:21).
